scope: Full visual supplement read of Parallellization_report.pdf

copy_comparison.fact: The source_code and manuals report copies have the same byte length and SHA-256, so the visual read applies to both paths.

method.visual: pdftoppm 24.02.0 rendered every physical page at 140 dpi to PNG; all 14 PNGs were opened at original detail and visually read.
method.text_aid: pdftotext -layout was used only as a navigation/checking aid; its Type 3 font extraction systematically drops characters and is not authoritative.
method.prior_conversion_problem: The 623-line Markdown conversion contains 41 image placeholders and sparse plot/table text, so it was insufficient as full-page evidence.

page_records.content: Title, authors/date, abstract, and contents. Abstract says typical runs take hours to days and motivates parallelization.
Continued contents; legacy main-step list: timestep, wave_bc, flow_bc, wave_stationary/wave_timestep, flow_timestep, transus, bed_update, varoutput; domain-decomposition motivation.
Reorganization into Fortran modules; code generation for housekeeping; 3x4/12-process two-dimensional domain decomposition diagram.
One-cell overlapping halos and neighbor relationships; master-only input/output description, broadcast versus divide/distribute, and collect-before-output.

Processor-grid selection minimizing total communication-edge length; xmpi_shift abstraction; need to refresh borders after local updates; scalability test setup (101x501, OpenMPI 1.2.6, gfortran, about 5-minute serial test).
Two speedup plots: one process per node and two processes per node, compared with ideal speedup; visible curves become sublinear and irregular at higher process counts.
Eight-core-node speedup plot; report conclusion claims usable scaling to 40 processes and speedup about 20 for the test model; technical conventions begin with USEMPI guards.

Conventions: use halt_program instead of stop; serial fallback values for xmpi_* variables; master-only I/O followed by broadcast; readkey_int/readkey_dbl described as MPI-aware while generic readkey needs master guard.
sglobal versus slocal model and boundary-update code-spotting patterns; MPI helper families separated among general_mpi.F90, xmpi.F90, and spaceparams.F90.
Tables of general_mpi, xmpi, and spaceparams helper roles; describes makeincludes generator for distributing and visiting more than 100 state variables.
Generated-file inventory for declarations, allocation, mnemonic/name-index lookup, and pointer access; demo.F90 mentioned as example.
Fortran assumed-shape/section buffer cautions for MPI_Bcast and nonblocking MPI_Isend/Irecv, including temporary-copy lifetime hazard.
Continuation recommends explicit contiguous copy for nonblocking sends; Scatterv displacement warning; historical Linux compile instructions and USEMPI/USEMPE/F90 macros.
Historical make targets and OpenMPI/MPICH2 eight-process launch examples.

document_claims_relevant_to_lifecycle.claim: The 2008 design describes one master process performing input/output, broadcast/distribution of state, and collection before output.
The document treats USEMPI guards, xmpi_initialize/finalize, halt_program, xmpi collectives/shifts, and serial xmpi constants as the intended parallel interface.

The report's sglobal/slocal description matches the broad current-source state split, but its single master-I/O description predates the current source's distinct xomaster output rank and therefore cannot establish the current call graph by itself.
The report's named main routines and build commands are historical names/instructions and must not override current definitions and checked manifests.

not_seen_or_not_claimed: No physical PDF page was skipped; pages 1-14 were visually opened and read.
Individual plotted marker coordinates were not digitized; only axes, legends, captions, trends, and stated conclusions were read.
The many pdftoppm Type 3 glyph bounding-box warnings did not prevent visible page rendering, but render hashes are tool/version-specific derivatives and do not replace the original PDF SHA.
This read does not prove that the 2008 build or runtime behavior remains active in the current source tree.
